acceptance_criteria: Incident-breaker state is staged privately and exclusively, fsynced before publication, and followed by required parent-directory fsync.
Corrupt or unavailable breaker state cannot silently reset tripped or escalation markers.
Process-lock payload is fsynced before it becomes authoritative.
Successful lock publication and authoritative unlink, reclaim, and release operations durably update the containing directory.
Existing hard-link exclusion, boot identity, ownership-checked unlink, and race behavior remain intact.
Focused tests assert ordering, permissions, cleanup, corruption behavior, and failures at pre- and post-publication boundaries.
blast_radius: Crash durability and fail-safe recovery for private incident-breaker and process-lock control state.
evidence_summary: Three stable body-free identity reads and matching API and SSH main reads established the current title, labels, timestamp, body SHA-256, and exact pin. Incident-breaker uses one fixed sibling .tmp name, default creation permissions, writeFileSync, and renameSync without file or parent-directory fsync; corrupt persisted state is converted to a fresh untripped and unescalated state. Process-lock uses an exclusive mode-0600 temporary payload and atomic hard-link publication, but it does not fsync the payload before linking or the parent directory after authoritative namespace changes. Private-fs is the positive control and implements private exclusive staging, file fsync, atomic rename, and parent-directory fsync with ordering tests. Existing incident-breaker and process-lock tests cover logical persistence, exclusion, ownership, corruption, races, and reclaim behavior but not the required crash-durability ordering. falsifier_or_remaining_gap: A current implementation that proves private exclusive staging, file fsync before rename or link, durable parent namespace updates, and fail-safe corruption handling with deterministic failure-boundary tests would falsify the finding. This audit did not perform a real power-loss experiment.
impact: A crash or power loss can lose or ambiguously publish safety state, while corrupt breaker state can silently reset trip and escalation markers that should remain fail-safe.
lead_verification_obligations: Approve the corruption policy and exact file and directory durability boundaries before implementation.
Run one forthcoming single stable complete open-pull-request census before assigning an implementation owner or recording overlaps.
Require deterministic failure injection for every pre-publication and post-publication operation while preserving lock exclusion and identity semantics.
suggested_remediation: Move incident-breaker persistence onto the established private atomic writer with fail-safe corruption behavior. Preserve process-lock hard-link exclusion while fsyncing its payload before link publication and durably syncing authoritative parent-directory changes.
title: durability: incident-breaker and process-lock state lack validated crash-safe persistence
